correctness.rationale: For every prime p >= 7 congruent 3 mod 4 the quadratic-residue Fourier frame is Parseval by orthogonality. The normalized quadratic Gauss sum yields the exact Hermitian Paley compression. All four possible tournament score sequences give three characteristic polynomials, formally verified using only integer-ring determinant expansion at an indeterminate p. Double regularity counts all isomorphism types. Polynomial subtraction at the respective largest roots and a direct root bracket establish strict strongest-erasure type, sharp operator bound and positivity. Exact finite cases were replayed from the actual standalone checker; they corroborate but are not substituted for the unrestricted proof. No unproved operator comparison or numerical-limit assumption is used.

value.rationale: The exact worst-case four-erasure lower bound for a natural Paley harmonic Parseval frame is a motivated quantitative robustness invariant not recoverable from ETF coherence alone. The complete three-polynomial compression spectrum, strict optimum at strong tournament geometry and exact count of equality patterns give parameter-uniform answers in all primes p=3 mod 4, including the p=7 boundary. This is more than a routine reexpression of the already-known transitive-four count, and its arithmetic spectra can inform adversarial Fourier sampling design.
